overall: The AG found the Committee violated the OML by posting its June 9 notice only on the Town Hall board, not at the official location, since the town had not adopted its website; other claims were dismissed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 9 meeting notice was not posted at the designated location and/or was not timely posted.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when it failed to post notice for its June 9 meeting in a manner conspicuously visible to the public at all hours in or on the municipal building in which the clerk’s office is located.

allegations.summary: Whether the notice was posted at least 48 hours before the meeting, as the website posting was made shortly before the June 7 deadline.
allegations.key_passage: It does appear that the meeting notice was posted to the website more than 48 hours in advance, even if just by minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant objected to topics listed on the notice and to spelling errors in it, claiming the topics were not adequately specific.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that a reasonable member of the public could have understood the nature of the Committee’s anticipated topics of discussion as listed, spelling mistakes notwithstanding.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised other grievances, including failure to report progress, removal of bike lanes, and general misconduct, which the AG said fall outside the OML.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee’s alleged failure to report its progress and its elimination of bike lanes, for example, do not implicate Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
